Question: In a room containing \(N\) people, \(N\gt3,\) at least one person has not shaken hands with everyone else in the room. What is the maximum number of people in the room that could have shaken hands with everyone else?
Solution:
A handshake involves two people, so one missing handshake prevents both people from having shaken hands with everyone.

Choose a person \(U\) who has not shaken hands with everyone, and choose someone \(V\) whose hand \(U\) has not shaken. Neither \(U\) nor \(V\) has shaken hands with everyone else. Therefore at most \(N-2\) people can have done so.

This bound is attainable: let every pair shake hands except the pair \(U,V\). Each of the other \(N-2\) people has then shaken hands with everyone else, while \(U\) and \(V\) have not.

Thus the maximum is \(\boxed{N-2}\). Since \(N>3\), this is at least \(2\) and is different from \(N-1\) and \(N\), so none of choices A through D gives the maximum. The answer is choice E.
